concepts.title: T-SQL query surface
concepts.definition: A query written in Transact-SQL and executed against a warehouse or a SQL analytics endpoint; the available objects and effective permissions come from that SQL surface.

concepts.title: KQL query
concepts.definition: A Kusto Query Language query executed in a KQL queryset against KQL data, typically tables in a KQL database hosted by an Eventhouse.

concepts.title: Calculation group
concepts.definition: A model object whose calculation items apply a DAX expression, such as a time-intelligence variant, to the measures that a visual selects.

concepts.title: Dynamic format string
concepts.definition: A measure or calculation-item format string supplied by a DAX expression, so the displayed format can follow the filter context instead of being fixed in the model.

concepts.title: Field parameter
concepts.definition: A model table of field references driven by a slicer, so a report consumer changes which column or measure a visual uses without editing the visual.

concepts.title: Composite model
concepts.definition: A semantic model whose tables use more than one storage mode, for example Import tables combined with DirectQuery or Direct Lake tables.

concepts.title: Incremental refresh
concepts.definition: A refresh policy that partitions an import-mode table and refreshes only the partitions inside a bounded window, so historical partitions are not reloaded on every refresh.

concepts.title: XMLA endpoint
concepts.definition: A Tabular-model endpoint that lets supported external tools read and, when enabled, write semantic model metadata for management and deployment.

concepts.title: Large semantic model storage format
concepts.definition: A storage format setting for semantic models that need more memory, recommended when models are written to through the XMLA endpoint.

concepts.title: Object-level security
concepts.definition: Model-role rules that hide specified tables or columns from a role, so affected users cannot see the object in reports or queries.

concepts.title: Warehouse column-level security
concepts.definition: Column permissions granted or denied with T-SQL on warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint objects; enforcement happens in the SQL engine rather than in the semantic model.

concepts.title: Warehouse row-level security
concepts.definition: A security predicate defined on a warehouse table that filters which rows a user can read through the SQL engine.

concepts.title: Workspace role
concepts.definition: A role such as Admin, Member, Contributor or Viewer that grants a user permissions on the items contained in a workspace.

concepts.title: Lineage and impact analysis
concepts.definition: The dependency view that shows how workspace items derive from one another, used to identify downstream consumers before a change is made.

semanticEdges.claim: A warehouse is queried with T-SQL through the SQL query editor.
semanticEdges.conditions: A supported warehouse item and a caller holding the SQL permissions the query needs; object availability follows the warehouse schema.
semanticEdges.rationale: The query documentation presents the warehouse SQL query editor as the T-SQL path for reading warehouse tables.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: A SQL analytics endpoint is also queried with T-SQL.
semanticEdges.conditions: The endpoint of a supported item; which tables are queryable depends on the item and on eligible shortcuts or tables, not on the SQL language itself.
semanticEdges.rationale: The documented T-SQL path covers a warehouse and a SQL analytics endpoint together, which makes the two surfaces easy to confuse when choosing a data store.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: T-SQL and KQL are different languages over different Fabric engines.
semanticEdges.conditions: T-SQL targets warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint objects; KQL targets KQL databases and querysets. Neither language substitutes for the other engine's data store.
semanticEdges.rationale: Both languages select, filter and aggregate, so the choice follows the data store and engine requirement rather than personal familiarity.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: An Eventhouse hosts KQL databases whose tables are queried with KQL in a KQL queryset.
semanticEdges.conditions: A KQL database in the Eventhouse plus the authorization needed to open the queryset and read the source tables.
semanticEdges.rationale: The KQL queryset is documented as the item used to run queries against data from an Eventhouse or a KQL database.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: A calculation item replaces the selected measure inside a DAX expression, so CALCULATE and filter-context reasoning are prerequisites.
semanticEdges.conditions: A model that supports calculation groups; the item only affects measures reached through SELECTEDMEASURE, not every measure in the model.
semanticEdges.rationale: The item body is a DAX expression evaluated for the measures in scope, so a result that ignores the visual's filters looks arbitrary without context reasoning.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: Dynamic format strings can be applied to calculation groups as well as to single measures.
semanticEdges.conditions: Scope differs: a calculation-group format applies to every measure the item affects, while a measure-level dynamic format stays limited to that one measure.
semanticEdges.rationale: The dynamic format string documentation states that the same DAX patterns apply, with the scope limited to individual measures instead of all measures in the model.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: Field parameters and calculation groups are adjacent ways to let a consumer change what a visual shows.
semanticEdges.conditions: A field parameter changes which field or measure a visual uses; a calculation group changes which calculation is applied to the measure already in the visual. Requirements usually need one of the two, not both.
semanticEdges.rationale: Both features solve a selection problem with a different model object, so combining them without a stated requirement adds maintenance cost without extra capability.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: A composite model combines Import tables with DirectQuery or Direct Lake tables.
semanticEdges.conditions: Supported combinations differ by authoring surface: Import can combine with DirectQuery, Dual and Direct Lake, while some Direct Lake combinations require web modeling or XMLA tools.
semanticEdges.rationale: The storage-mode comparison lists which pairings each mode supports, so the label 'composite' alone does not state which modes are combined or where that pairing can be authored.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: Import storage creates model table partitions, and an incremental refresh policy refreshes only the partitions inside its window.
semanticEdges.conditions: The table needs the date parameters and filter the policy expects; partitions are created when the policy is published and the model is refreshed, not at authoring time.
semanticEdges.rationale: The storage-mode comparison attributes automatic model table partitions to incremental refresh in Import mode, and to the XMLA endpoint when partitions are created manually.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: An incremental refresh policy and Direct Lake describe different refresh mechanisms.
semanticEdges.conditions: Direct Lake exposes no model table partitions; partitioning can be done at the Delta table level instead, so an import partition policy is not the equivalent control.
semanticEdges.rationale: Expecting partition policies from Direct Lake leads to a refresh design that the storage mode does not provide; freshness depends on the Delta tables rather than on import partitions.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: The XMLA endpoint lets supported external tools deploy and manage semantic models, complementing workspace deployment pipelines.
semanticEdges.conditions: Read-write XMLA must be enabled for the capacity and the caller needs the required permissions. Pipelines promote workspace items; XMLA operates on semantic model metadata.
semanticEdges.rationale: The two paths overlap for semantic models but differ in scope and in what they can change, so neither one replaces the other.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: Enabling the large semantic model storage format is recommended for models that are written to through the XMLA endpoint.
semanticEdges.conditions: Applies to capacities that support large models; the setting changes memory and management behavior and is not a general performance fix for every model.
semanticEdges.rationale: The XMLA documentation links write operations to enabling large models, so the storage format decision and the write path are reviewed together.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: Object-level security hides tables and columns, while row-level security filters rows; both are defined in model roles.
semanticEdges.conditions: Both depend on role membership and on the identity used to query the model; neither restricts a consumer who has an independent path to the source data.
semanticEdges.rationale: The OLS documentation places both features in model roles but they restrict different things, so satisfying one requirement does not satisfy the other.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: Column restrictions can be enforced in the SQL engine or in the semantic model.
semanticEdges.conditions: Warehouse column-level security uses T-SQL grants on Warehouse or SQL analytics endpoint objects; model OLS uses model roles. The two rule sets are separate and must both be reviewed.
semanticEdges.rationale: The same column can be protected twice, and a consumer that reads the data directly does not inherit the model's object-level rule.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: Row filtering can be defined as a SQL predicate or as a model role written in DAX.
semanticEdges.conditions: Warehouse RLS applies to queries on the warehouse table; model RLS applies to consumers of the semantic model. A Power BI query on a warehouse in Direct Lake mode falls back to DirectQuery to abide by the warehouse rule.
semanticEdges.rationale: Both restrict rows but at different layers, so a consumer with direct warehouse access is not filtered by the model's RLS roles.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: A column-level security rule on a warehouse forces a Direct Lake query to fall back to DirectQuery.
semanticEdges.conditions: Documented for Power BI queries on a warehouse in Direct Lake mode; the fallback preserves the restriction at a performance cost, so the rule and the storage mode are chosen together.
semanticEdges.rationale: Security and performance are coupled in this case: removing the column rule is not a tuning step, and accepting the fallback is a deliberate trade-off.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: A workspace role grants access to items, while RLS decides which rows a model consumer can see.
semanticEdges.conditions: Workspace Admin, Member and Contributor roles have edit permission on the semantic model, so RLS does not apply to them; Viewers are subject to the model's RLS roles even when they can build reports.
semanticEdges.rationale: Item access and data filtering are separate decisions, so a broad workspace role is not a substitute for a row-level rule.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

semanticEdges.claim: Lineage shows item dependencies while the monitoring hub shows job executions; both inform a change decision.
semanticEdges.conditions: Lineage visibility depends on workspace permissions, and the monitoring hub covers job activity rather than data-flow dependencies.
semanticEdges.rationale: One view answers what depends on an item, the other answers whether its runs succeeded; a change review needs both questions answered.
semanticEdges.reviewer: Agent documentation review 2026-10-26; not human approval

coverage.basis: Skills measured as of October 19, 2026; official pages checked 2026-10-26
coverage.scope: Second expansion layer. Covers SQL/KQL querying, calculation groups, dynamic format strings, field parameters, composite models, incremental refresh, XMLA and large models, and layered security. Still not exhaustive: DAX iterator/window functions, workspace and item access variants, sensitivity labels, .pbip and .pbit assets, denormalization and aggregation patterns, and question-level scientific review remain open.
